main.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II
main.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II is a 2022 first-person shooter game developed by Infinity Ward and published by Activision.

cards.heading: The sequel to the Modern Warfare reboot
cards.text: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II is a 2022 first-person shooter game developed by Infinity Ward and published by Activision. It is the nineteenth installment of the Call of Duty series, serving as a sequel to the 2019 reboot of the Modern Warfare sub-series. The game was released on October 28, 2022, for PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Windows, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S.

cards.heading: Task Force 141 and a shared ecosystem
cards.text: Like its predecessor, the game takes place in a realistic and modern setting. The campaign follows multi-national special operations unit Task Force 141 and Mexican Special Forces unit Los Vaqueros as they attempt to track down terrorist leader Hassan Zyani, who is in possession of American-made ballistic missiles. Powered by a new version of the IW engine, Modern Warfare II continues to support cross-platform multiplayer. It also shares the Call of Duty HQ launcher ecosystem with Warzone 2.0, the free-to-play follow-up to the original Warzone, released separately on November 16, 2022.

cards.heading: Commercial success and another sequel
cards.text: Modern Warfare II received generally favorable reviews from critics. It was a commercial success and broke several records for the series, including becoming the fastest Call of Duty game to generate US$1 billion in revenue. A sequel, titled Modern Warfare III, was released on November 10, 2023.

main.title: Sonic Frontiers
main.summary: Sonic Frontiers is a 2022 platform game developed by Sonic Team and published by Sega for the Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Windows, Xbox One and Xbox Series X/S.

cards.heading: Sonic reaches the Starfall Islands
cards.text: Sonic Frontiers is a 2022 platform game developed by Sonic Team and published by Sega for the Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Windows, Xbox One and Xbox Series X/S. Its story follows Sonic the Hedgehog and his friends, who after falling into a wormhole are left stranded in an artificial dimension of the Starfall Islands known as Cyber Space. Sonic escapes the dimension and sets off on a mission to rescue his trapped allies by defeating the islands' "Titans". Combining traditional Sonic the Hedgehog series elements with an open world structure, the gameplay of Frontiers sees the player controlling Sonic through the islands in order to collect the Chaos Emeralds, which are necessary to defeat the Titans. This is accomplished by completing various challenges strewn throughout that test the player through platforming, puzzle solving or combat encounters.

cards.heading: Speed, rings and new abilities
cards.text: Sonic explores the Starfall Islands with familiar jumps, rails, rings and homing attacks, joined by new combat moves and the Cyloop. Running a closed trail around an object can trigger an interaction, while particular shapes provide temporary advantages such as sustained boost. Energy still limits speed, and collecting the maximum number of rings offers another period of unlimited boosting. Players can adjust acceleration, turning and other controls as well as difficulty. Upgrades develop attack, defence and movement capacities, giving the open areas reasons to revisit a route after learning more of Sonic's abilities.

cards.heading: An open zone full of challenges
cards.text: The islands combine open exploration with rails, springs and boost pads. Puzzles reveal sections of the map and provide items needed to reach Sonic's friends, who are trapped in Cyber Space. Their holographic appearances allow conversations and requests even before they are freed. Kocos, seeds and tokens support different improvements or story encounters, turning a detour into another kind of progress. Later updates added music memories and Action Chain Challenges. Earning top ranks in all of those challenges unlocks the Spin Dash, giving familiar terrain another movement technique to explore.

cards.heading: Robots, Guardians and new combat moves
cards.text: The player battles robots throughout the islands, all in various forms; Sonic can dodge and parry attacks and use the Cyloop to make enemies easier to strike. Defeating enemies grants the player experience points that allow the player to purchase additional moves and abilities in combat and the open world. Alongside regular, small enemies, the player battles large "Guardian" bosses. Defeating a Guardian rewards the player with portal gears that, when placed in a portal, allow them to enter Cyber Space.

main.title: God of War Ragnarök
main.subtitle: Kratos and Atreus face Ragnarok
main.summary: God of War Ragnarök is a 2022 action-adventure game developed by Santa Monica Studio and published by Sony Interactive Entertainment.

cards.heading: Kratos and Atreus face Ragnarok
cards.text: God of War Ragnarök is a 2022 action-adventure game developed by Santa Monica Studio and published by Sony Interactive Entertainment. It was released worldwide on November 9, 2022, for both the PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5, marking the first cross-generation release in the God of War series, and was released for Windows on September 19, 2024. It is the ninth installment in the series, the tenth chronologically, and the sequel to 2018's God of War. Loosely based on Norse mythology, the game is set in mythical ancient Scandinavia and features series protagonist, Kratos, and his now teenage son, Atreus. Concluding the Norse era of the series, the story follows Kratos and Atreus' efforts to prevent the nine realms from being destroyed by Ragnarök, the eschatological event which is central to Norse mythology and was foretold to happen in the previous game after Kratos killed the Aesir god Baldur.

cards.heading: New weapons and a playable Atreus
cards.text: The gameplay is similar to the previous 2018 installment. It features combo-based combat, as well as puzzle and role-playing elements. Improvements and additions include Kratos' main weapons: a magical battle axe and his double-chained blades, and a new magical spear; his shield has become more versatile, with different types of shields that have differing offensive and defensive abilities. His son Atreus, as well as some other characters, provide assistance in combat and can be passively controlled, though as a new feature in the series, Atreus is fully controllable in specific story segments.

cards.heading: A delayed release and the Valhalla epilogue
cards.text: Originally slated for a 2021 release, the game was delayed in part due to Kratos actor Christopher Judge's health problems in August 2019, and later, the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on development. A free expansion pack, Valhalla, was released on December 12, 2023. Featuring roguelite gameplay and serving as an epilogue to Ragnarök, it follows Kratos as he participates in a series of trials within Valhalla, where he must come to terms with his past life in Greece.

cards.heading: Reception and awards
cards.text: Ragnarök received critical acclaim, with critics praising its storytelling, characters, emotional weight, visuals, level design, and quality of life improvements over its predecessor. Minor criticism focused on narrative pacing, certain gameplay mechanics, as well as the excessive hints during puzzles. The game sold 5.1 million units in its first week, making it the fastest-selling first-party launch week in PlayStation history, with over 15 million units sold by November 2023. At the Game Awards 2022, Ragnarök received a leading 11 nominations, including Game of the Year, winning six. It received a leading 12 nominations at the 26th Annual D.I.C.E. Awards, ultimately winning seven awards including Adventure Game of the Year. It also received a leading 15 nominations at the 19th British Academy Games Awards, the most nominations for any game in the history of the ceremony, from which it won six awards, including the EE Game of the Year Award.

main.title: Atari 50
main.subtitle: Atari's 50th anniversary becomes a playable documentary
main.summary: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration is a 2022 video game compilation and interactive documentary developed by Digital Eclipse and published by Atari to commemorate the 50th anniversary of Atari, Inc.

cards.heading: Atari's 50th anniversary becomes a playable documentary
cards.text: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration is a 2022 video game compilation and interactive documentary developed by Digital Eclipse and published by Atari to commemorate the 50th anniversary of Atari, Inc. It is composed of newly shot interviews with former Atari employees, archival footage, emulated games from the company's catalog, and six new games inspired by various Atari games. It was released for the Atari VCS, Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Windows, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S on November 11, 2022.

cards.heading: A five-part timeline connects archives and games
cards.text: The game is presented as a five-part interactive timeline that lays out the history of the company and its products through video, scanned artifacts and related games. It received generally favorable reviews, with critics comparing it favorably to a museum or traditional documentary. They praised its thoroughness and hoped other developers would receive a similar treatment.

cards.heading: More games and a Gold Master Series
cards.text: Since its release, Digital Eclipse has added additional games as free updates and paid downloadable content, later compiled into Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration Expanded Edition. The success of the game led Digital Eclipse to develop additional documentary-style game compilations, known as the Gold Master Series.

main.title: Pentiment
main.subtitle: A Videogame That Thinks Like an Annotated Page
main.summary: Pentiment's sixteenth-century Germany is defined by the transition between manuscript culture and print.

cards.heading: A Videogame That Thinks Like an Annotated Page
cards.text: Obsidian's Pentiment follows Andreas Maler through murder investigations in sixteenth-century Germany. Its illustrated-book presentation draws on manuscripts, woodcuts and print. Typefaces change with a speaker's education and social position, while visible corrections suggest words written on a page. Documents and personal memories shape what Andreas learns about the community.

cards.heading: Writing Reveals Who Is Speaking
cards.text: Characters use different scripts associated with their education, profession and surroundings. Words appear as if written by hand, sometimes with a mistake crossed out and corrected. The form of the dialogue supplies information about a speaker alongside the sentence itself. Reading the page also becomes a way of recognising the person speaking.

cards.heading: Manuscript and Print Coexist in the Same World
cards.text: Manuscript work and printing coexist in Andreas's world. Scriptoria, woodcuts, workshops and religious texts connect changes in communication to daily occupations. New production techniques affect who can make a text and how widely it can travel. These changes emerge through people, jobs and objects encountered during the investigation.

cards.heading: The Community Decides What Remains Written
cards.text: Investigation takes place under time pressure, with partial testimony and consequences that last for years. Documents and spoken accounts may disagree. Andreas's decisions affect people who continue living in the town, and later recollections absorb those events. What the community remembers depends partly on the information preserved and the choices made from it.
